title: The role of local and systemic inflammation in inflammatory bowel disease, autoimmune disease, and cardiometabolic disease.
summary:
In the context of inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD), autoimmune diseases (e.g. multiple sclerosis (MS)/neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders (NMOSD) or diabetes mellitus) and cardiovascular diseases, first correlations between inflammatory processes and alterations of the intestinal microbiota (dysbiosis) have been described. There exists a bidirectional dependency with altered microbial metabolite- in the gut and consequently in the systemic circulation of patients*. It is unclear to what extent these early local changes play a role in pathogenesis, treatment response or further disease progression. It is also unclear whether there are possible biomarkers or cross-disease mechanisms in this context.

The subject of the present pilot study is a cross-disease, multidimensional approach. The focus is on multiple disease entities and the effect of their inflammatory status on intestinal microbiota, immune system, and vascular endothelial function. This study will contribute to a better understanding of the importance and impact of dysbiosis, as well as identify potential biomarkers for the respective disease progression and potential therapeutic response. 

Biopsies of intestinal tissue, a comprehensive analysis of blood and stool samples, as well as examinations of cardiac and vascular function are carried out according to standardized protocols on patients with IBD (Ulcerative Colitis and Crohn's Disease), MS, diabetes, hypertension, metabolic syndrome, or heart failure. A group of healthy subjects undergoing regular colorectal cancer screening will serve as a control.

interventions.name: Patients with histologically confirmed Ulcerative colitis
Patients with histologically confirmed Crohn's disease
Patients with heart failure (according to ESC Guidelines 2021)
Patients with hypertension (diagnostic criteria according to International Society of Hypertension Global Hypertension Practice Guidelines, 2020)
Patients with multiple sclerosis (diagnostic criteria according to McDonald)
Healthy subjects who routinely undergo a colonoscopy

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Disease definition according to guidelines: 
- Ulcerative Colitis or Crohn's Disease, histologically confirmed
- Heart Failure: ESC Guidelines 2021
- Metabolic Syndrome
- Diabetes: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with or without insulin therapy
- MS: Diagnosis according to McDonald 2017, Ref. Thompson et al. Lancet Neurol 2017
- Hypertension: Unger et al 2020 ‘2020 International Society of Hypertension Global Hypertension Practice Guidelines’ Hypertension. 2020;75:1334–1357
Exclusion criteria:
- Refusal to participate in the study 
- Lack of capacity to give consent 
- Pregnancy and/or active breastfeeding
